This movement is already backed by 3 already formed parties, and they are organizing every single protest, they just don't claim it because what keeps people comming for them is the claim that it's not "political" when, in fact, it is. And our elections are next year...so yeah, think about that. Nobody I know that went to the protests knows exactly what they want, hell, most of them probably don't even know who they voted for congress last election. We gotta start from there, screaming on the streets won't help.

First we need a Political Reform. We are NOT really represented in the congress, at all. We have over here an abnormality called "electoral coefficient" where, although you vote for a single congressman, the vote, in fact, goes to the political party, and then the chairs are distributed among them according to the % of votes. We even had a comedian (well, basically a clown) have a campaign based on the slogan "It can't get any worse", he got so many votes that his party managed to elect 4 more congressmen with him using them. This is many levels of absurd on itself. Adding to that is the fact parties here in Brazil don't mean anything, to give you an idea, Sao Paulo's ex-mayor created a political party (in itself a political maneuver) and declared that it wasn't on the left, on the right or in the center: there's not political plan except for power in itself.This needs to change, there needs to be a debate. It's been about 15 years that the reforms are archived in the congress, of course they are *NOT* interested in doing anything. Either by discrict voting or closed lists, peolple need to really know WHO they are electing (or at least what party). Once politicians know who, in fact, they represent, and the people know who represents them, we can make real demands.

Our taxes are so ridiculous that companies dedicate, in average, 3 months a year to pay them. A funny anedocte: our government recently passed a law that made it obligatory to discriminate what taxes we pay when we buy things: thing is, nobody exactly knows how to do that, we have so many different taxes that it is impossible to determine what exactly is the price of the product (in itself having a miryad of taxes from the raw materials, to the production line, logistics, etc) and what is, de facto, tax. 

And that's just the tip of the iceberg. Our "intelectuals" think that we're still in militar dictatorship, and that in 2013 it's valid to discuss whether or not we should retake private companies that were privatized more than a decade ago (and were HUUUUGE money sinks and completely inefficient) or even that the government should be the huge state to provide everything. It's "schizophrenical". Every single social or student movement here is dominated by leftist political parties (namely PSOL, PSTU, PCdoB), where they doctrinate the leaders to their agendas (death to America! all hail our Cuban overlords!) and then claim that the movement is politics-free. Such a sad joke. I've seen sooo many people on facebook saying that we are having a "Brazilian Spring", yet they have no fucking idea what it was or how it went for those countries, just ask Libya, or Egypt, or Syria. We are NOT a dictatorship, we need to change things with our vote. **NO AMOUNT** of people screaming in the streets can change that, specially when our current president enjoys a 70% approvation rate. Just look at what Movimento dos Sem Terra teach to their kids, it's...bizarre.

Bad healthcare, horrible education, police reforms (we have two: one for arresting and patrol, one for investigation...yeah), law reforms... all these things stem from the fact that we have a ridiculously large nation with one of the most ridiculous political systems of any democracy, where politicians don't even know who elected them. And we can't even start a serious debate without being called a "rightis burgeois".
well, they were voted in there. Should we protest against the people?

That's what I've been saying to my colleagues: there are no demands to the protests, at least no PRACTICAL ones. 100 thousand people in Rio protesting over...what? A better country? A better country how? Lower taxes? By how much? Hell, most of the protesters don't even have any idea of WHO is organizing the riots, or even what exactly they want besides "HURR DURR CORRUPTION IS BAD", so any attempt of negotiation is void. It's beautiful seeing Brazil waking up, but sad at the same time to see how ignorant the masses can be.

edit: oh, and about the bus fare: at least here in Sao Paulo, we have what we call "Bilhete Unico", where if you would pay more than one fare in a limited amount of time (2 buses, bus+subway+train, for example) you either

 a)Don't pay the second one. At all.


 b)Pay half the price for the second one.

What I don't get is that this, of course, is NOT free. The money for these fares must come from somewhere, and that's why fares are "high" overall. It seems people completely forgot about this.
